title: One-variable statistics
purpose: Type a list of numbers one at a time and press enter on a blank line to finish. The calculator returns the count, sum, mean, five-number summary, IQR, range, and both standard deviations.
formula:
mean = sum(x) / n
sigx = sqrt(SS / n)      population
sx   = sqrt(SS / (n-1))  sample
  where SS = sum (x - mean)^2
Q1 = median of values below the median
prompts: x1, x2, x3 ... one value per prompt, in any order
Press enter on an empty line to finish the list
outputs: n = how many values, sum, mean
min, Q1, med, Q3, max - the five-number summary
IQR = Q3 - Q1, and rnge = max - min
sigx = population SD, sx = sample SD
quirks: An EMPTY line ends the list. Just press enter with nothing typed.
Values may be entered in any order - the program sorts them itself.

Quartiles use the same convention as the calculator's built-in 1-Var Stats: Q1 is the median of the values below the median, excluding the median itself when n is odd. Some textbooks use a different rule and will disagree slightly.
sx is the SAMPLE standard deviation (divide by n-1); sigx is the POPULATION one (divide by n). Check which your exercise wants.
With one value only, sx prints n/a - a sample SD needs at least two.
Negatives, decimals and a decimal comma all work: -3 and 2,5 are fine.
A typo prints "Not a number" and re-asks without losing the list so far.
mode_note: Mode does not matter. STATS1 only does arithmetic and square roots, so the DEGREE / RADIAN setting has no effect on it.
